Biosimilars could slash drug costs, but Big Pharma’s patent games and Medicare’s broken payment models block progress. The Senate Judiciary Committee just advanced the Preserve Access to Affordable Generics and Biosimilars Act (S.1096) to crack down on tactics like “product hopping” – where companies tweak drugs to extend monopolies. Case in point: Merck’s Keytruda scheme to shift to subcutaneous versions before patent expiry, locking out competition until 2028. 

Meanwhile, Medicare Part B’s reimbursement structure still favors expensive biologics over biosimilars, with payment rates tied to brand-name drug prices. Fixing this requires overhauling the Average Sales Price calculation to remove perverse incentives. Until Washington stops letting Pharma exploit 130+ patent thickets per drug (see inhalers: $111B in post-patent profits), patients will keep paying the price. 

Real reform means dismantling regulatory capture, not just tinkering with payment formulas.
